I fixed the bug. `s = "caf\u00e9"` now parses to `{'s': 'café'}`.

The cause was in `parse_hex_char` in `src/tomli/_parser.py`. After reading the hex digits of a `\x`, `\u` or `\U` escape, it advanced the position by `hex_len - 1`. That left the parser on the last hex digit, so the digit was read a second time as a normal character, which gave `café9`. It now advances by `hex_len`.

I checked `\U0001F600x`, which parses to `😀x`. With `PYTHONPATH=src`, the test suite gives 17 passed and 1 skipped. Without it, pytest can't import `tomli` and stops with collection errors. I didn't add a regression test for this.
